chunks: And as for what was narrated: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Sahl from Muhammad ibn Mansur al-Kufi said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him) about a boy who plays with a slave-girl whom he does not own and has not reached puberty, is it permissible for his father to buy her and touch her? He said, 'That which is forbidden does not make the permissible forbidden.'

This is also not contradictory to what we have previously stated, because his saying 'plays with a slave-girl' may be a reference to something other than sexual intercourse. As for with sexual intercourse, then she becomes forbidden in all cases according to what we have previously stated. And whenever the father has a slave-girl whom he has not had intercourse with or touched in a manner that functions like intercourse, it is not objectionable for the son to have intercourse with her if he owns her.

key_terms.لَا يُحَرِّمُ الْحَرَامُ الْحَلَالَ: That which is forbidden does not make the permissible forbidden
key_terms.يَعْبَثُ: plays or engages in casual contact

ai.seo_question: Can a father and son both have intercourse with the same slave-girl?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes that a father’s prior possession of a slave-girl does not create a permanent prohibition for his son, citing the principle that 'that which is forbidden does not make the permissible forbidden.' This ruling is nuanced by distinguishing between general 'playing' (which may exclude intercourse) and actual sexual union, ensuring clarity in the application of consanguinity-like prohibitions within the context of slavery. The hadith underscores the flexibility of marital laws in Shia jurisprudence regarding shared ownership and prior intimate relations.
